evidence: instruction.md reads as a recruiting lead talking to a builder, not as generated spec prose. It opens with a question and a first-person framing: 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? Two things happen in it.' (line 1). The second sentence is a short fragment-like beat, and the line continues 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.' Sentence length varies from four words ('Candidates sign in too.' line 9) to long, run-on operational sentences (line 13). The brief uses idiomatic first-person asks: 'tell me why; when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who' (line 3), 'I often move several candidates together' (line 3), 'never touch my draft or my cursor' (line 7), 'layout and names are yours' (line 11), 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call' (line 13), and 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout' (line 11). Contractions counted with grep: don't x2, it's, mustn't, nobody's, people's. Grep for marketing or LLM gloss (seamless|robust|delve|leverage|intuitive|elevate|streamline|ensure|comprehensive|em dash) found zero hits in instruction.md and both notes. The brief has no bullets or numbered lists, so it has no perfectly parallel bullets. The notes keep the same speaker. hireops_rules.md speaks as 'our recruiting workspace' and says 'what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way this note says' (lines 3-5). It also includes 'Where drafts are kept is yours' (line 175) and short terse statements such as 'Identifiers are generated by the workspace.' (line 38) and 'A refused move changes nothing.' (line 53). Its tables and bullets fit a team rules note, which the skill expects to be terser and more rule-like. They are not the brief's main voice, and the bullets vary in length and structure rather than being templated. integration.md is the shared template note; diff shows the only change is an appended delivery paragraph. Its plain neutral register is template-controlled and is not an authoring voice defect. Plausible-failure probe: a reader might call instruction.md line 13 a build recipe because it lists the start command, port, health path and DB_PATH in one sentence. Even there the voice stays casual ('is your call', 'so don't install packages', 'if that helps'). Whether that runtime content suits a product ask belongs to rows 1 and 4, not to voice. Conforming-alternative probe: a terser rewrite would also pass, because the workbook says 'casual/terse is good'. Nothing in this row could penalise a correct submission, since the row grades only the authored text. Minor observation (P3, not a defect for this row): spelling varies between British and American forms. instruction.md line 13 uses 'honour PORT' and 'honouring DB_PATH', while hireops_rules.md line 201 uses 'Honor the supplied DB_PATH' and integration.md line 7 uses 'honoring'. This is a small seam between the brief and the task-authored rules note, not a change of voice; row 3 (spelling and contamination) owns it if the owner wants uniform spelling. No runtime or judge evidence is needed for this row, so raw-evidence-index.json was not relied on, and no Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
